methodological_rigor.justification: VIKTORIA-1 Study 1 is a global (147 sites in 23 countries), open-label, randomized phase III trial with 1:1:1 assignment (N=392) stratified by visceral metastasis, time to PD on prior therapy, and region. Primary endpoint (BICR-assessed PFS) is tested hierarchically (triplet vs fulvestrant first, then doublet vs fulvestrant) with prespecified alpha allocation (one-sided 0.025; interim OS alpha 0.000174/0.000173). Central PIK3CA testing with therascreen RGQ PCR. Crossover permitted with planned sensitivity analysis. IDMC oversight and AE grading per CTCAE v5.0. Limitations acknowledged (ESR1 not assessable, only palbociclib as CDK4/6i studied).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: In a common post-CDK4/6i HR+/HER2-/PIK3CA-WT population, the gedatolisib triplet vs fulvestrant HR 0.24 (95% CI 0.17-0.35) and doublet HR 0.33 represent practice-changing magnitude of benefit in a disease area with limited options. PAM pathway targeting in PIK3CA-WT disease represents a clinically important expansion beyond current biomarker-selected approvals (alpelisib, inavolisib). Individual RCT -> Oxford LoE 1b.

reporting_quality.justification: Full CONSORT-consistent reporting: randomization, stratification, eligibility, prespecified statistical plan with hierarchical alpha allocation, BICR adjudication, patient disposition figure, AE tables by group, and transparent discussion of limitations (including enrollment overage of 41 patients). Trial registration (NCT05501886) and ethics/IDMC oversight documented. Data availability statement not visible in normalized text.

novelty_literature.justification: First phase III trial to demonstrate clinically meaningful PFS benefit of a multitarget PAM inhibitor (all four class I PI3K isoforms plus mTORC1/2) in PIK3CA-WT HR+/HER2- ABC post-CDK4/6i, validating the PAM pathway as a driver even in PIK3CA-WT disease. Triplet regimen (PI3K/AKT/mTOR + CDK4/6 + ET) represents a new therapeutic paradigm with clinically superior PFS magnitude vs historical and contemporary second-line trials. High novelty for the field.

writing_presentation.justification: Manuscript is precise, well-organized, and candid about limitations. Clear presentation of primary and key secondary endpoints, subgroup analyses, and safety comparisons with historical PAM inhibitor data (SOLAR-1 alpelisib, BOLERO-2 everolimus, CAPItello-291 capivasertib). Stomatitis prophylaxis (SWISH) rationale is explicitly discussed. Figures and tables appropriately signposted.

key_strengths: Pivotal phase III RCT (N=392, 23 countries) with hierarchical alpha-controlled PFS primary endpoint
Large, clinically meaningful PFS benefit: triplet HR 0.24 and doublet HR 0.33 vs fulvestrant
Demonstrates PAM-pathway targeting benefit in PIK3CA-WT disease, broadening eligible population
Favorable tolerability vs single-node PAM inhibitors (hyperglycemia 9.2% vs 63.7% in SOLAR-1)
Prespecified subgroup and crossover-censored sensitivity analyses
key_concerns: OS interim immature and did not cross prespecified boundary (triplet HR 0.69; doublet 0.74)
Only palbociclib as CDK4/6i studied; abemaciclib/ribociclib combinations untested
Fulvestrant monotherapy control is no longer SOC in many regions
ESR1 mutation status not assessable due to sample constraints
Data availability statement not visible in normalized text
chief_reviewer.rationale: Large, rigorously designed phase III RCT with practice-changing PFS benefit and favorable safety profile in a clinically important setting; Tier 1 venues such as NEJM, Lancet Oncology, or JCO are appropriate.
